findings.current: Lead with the elbow, pour the pinky up.
findings.problem: Tipping the pinky up turns the arm further inward at the top of the raise, the position linked to shoulder impingement. The source cues the opposite: a slight outward turn as the arm nears shoulder height.
findings.corrected: Lead with the elbow and keep the thumb level with or slightly above the pinky.

findings.current: Trains the entire back line ... with zero equipment and zero spinal compression.
findings.problem: The 'zero spinal compression' claim is false. Measured at L4-5, active trunk extension produced the highest joint forces of the extensor exercises tested, and adding the opposite arm to a leg lift raised compression further.
findings.corrected: Trains the whole back line, the muscles that hold you upright, with no equipment. Keep the lift low; if your lower back complains, switch to the bird dog.
findings.sourceName: Callaghan, Gunning, McGill 1998, Physical Therapy: lumbar spine load and muscle activity during extensor exercises (Europe PMC record)

findings.current: The rotation hits all three shoulder heads in one move.
findings.problem: Not supported. The ACE-sponsored EMG study found no single exercise best for all three deltoid heads; presses lead for the front head, while the rear head needs rows or rear raises.
findings.corrected: The rotation adds range to a press that mainly trains the front and side of the shoulder. Pair it with a rear delt move.
findings.sourceName: ACE ProSource: Dynamite Delts, ACE research identifies top shoulder exercises

findings.problem: Mislabeled. The entry's own musclesWorked lists hamstrings, calves, shoulders and lats, and the source files the pose under arms, back, hips and legs, not abs.

A superman is not an easier step down: lifting trunk, arms and legs together is the highest-load version of floor extension work. The lower-load starting point is a single leg lift, then opposite arm and leg.
findings.corrected: Bird dog, or lying face down and lifting one leg at a time.
findings.sourceName: Callaghan, Gunning, McGill 1998, Physical Therapy: lumbar spine load and muscle activity during extensor exercises (Europe PMC record)

findings.problem: The steps tell the user to stand on an edge and drop the heels below it, so the lift as written needs a step or platform. Only the beginner version is done flat on the floor.
findings.corrected: Step or sturdy edge; dumbbells optional
